biography: Arnd Meier, a name synonymous with a certain… flamboyance in the German motorsport scene, hails from a small village nestled in the Black Forest. Unlike many of his peers who grew up karting, Arnd's introduction to speed came through illegal street racing in his youth. He honed his skills, or at least, his nerve, dodging Polizei in a souped-up BMW. It wasn't until a particularly close call with the authorities that he decided to channel his talents into something slightly less… jail-worthy. A wealthy local businessman, impressed by Arnd's reckless abandon, sponsored his entry into Formula Ford. While never a championship contender, Arnd carved out a respectable career as a midfield battler, known more for his audacious overtakes and occasional spectacular crashes than consistent results. Now in his late 30s, and after spending years in the Lola T98 Ford, Arnd acknowledges his time at the top is likely over, but he maintains he is still driving for the thrill.
drivingStyle: Meier's driving style can be best described as 'seat-of-the-pants'. He's not one for meticulous data analysis or subtle tire management. Instead, he relies on raw instinct and aggression, often throwing the car into corners with a breathtaking disregard for the laws of physics. This approach yields occasional flashes of brilliance, but also results in costly errors and strained relationships with his mechanics, who frequently find themselves piecing his car back together.

rivalries.name: Hans-Dieter Ziegler
rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision in a Formula 3 race, where Arnd accused Hans-Dieter of deliberately blocking him.

rivalries.name: Isabelle Dubois
rivalries.reason: A fierce on-track rivalry fueled by mutual respect and a desire to prove themselves against each other, often resulting in wheel-to-wheel battles.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: A rivalry sparked by Arnd publicly criticizing Kenji's driving style as 'too clinical' and lacking passion. Kenji responded with a series of sarcastic social media posts.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, even if they're full of holes.
Listens to German techno music at ear-splitting volume immediately before entering the car.
Insists on personally polishing his steering wheel before every race, claiming it improves grip.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. You drive to win, or you don't drive at all!"
careerHighlight: Winning the ADAC GT Masters race at the Nürburgring in 2012, a stunning victory achieved in pouring rain after starting from the back of the grid.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 24 Hours of Spa in 2015 due to a mechanical failure, costing his team a likely victory and significant championship points.
